subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should `GatewayClient` keep unlimited reconnects by default and expose only an opt-in cap for short-lived callers, or should OpenClaw change the default reconnect policy globally?
rationale: The source-level unbounded scheduler is clear, but node-host recovery intentionally benefits from indefinite reconnects, so the default retry contract is a compatibility and product decision.

options.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
options.body: Keep existing long-lived clients unlimited by default, add the cap to the package client, and wire it only into caller paths maintainers approve as short-lived.

options.title: Global retry cap
options.body: Stop every GatewayClient after a fixed number of attempts, accepting that node hosts may not recover automatically after extended gateway outages.

options.title: Document unlimited retry as intended
options.body: Keep the current retry model and close the report only if maintainers explicitly accept the resource-risk tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
recommendation.body: Keep existing long-lived clients unlimited by default, add the cap to the package client, and wire it only into caller paths maintainers approve as short-lived.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is tied to both the original Gateway WebSocket client and the package extraction, making them the best available owner for the reconnect contract decision.
